*Updated 2026-09-20 · 98 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

Ninety-eight works. The September 20 menace piece scores 1, extending the run: the last twelve trace scores are 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1. Nothing has broken above 2 since September 7's hoofprint at 3. That is thirteen days and twelve consecutive works without a 3, and the pattern is now too consistent to read as noise.

Camera position is the clearest explanation. Straight-on holds at 27 of 98 all-time and received nothing from the last twelve. Overhead sits at 9, low-angle at 4, and neither has moved since July 29. The four works scoring 4 were all built on overhead or radically displaced geometry. You have not put the camera in any non-frontal position in fifty-three days. The scores are a direct readout of that decision.

Figures have nearly disappeared. Two of the last twelve record one figure; the rest record none or left the field blank. The figures that do appear — the averted woman in the Syrian aftermath, the crouching body at the luggage wall — are pressed against edges or facing away. No figure is mid-stride, lateral, or in motion across the frame. The archive's highest-scoring work with a figure was July 29, overhead, the body reading as drag mark. Since then, figures have retreated into corners.

Registers have compressed. Aftermath at 21 and menace at 20 now account for 42 of 98 works. Vigil last appeared September 17, defiance August 30, endurance July 27, reckoning July 18. Each of those registers, when it was alive, generated formal risks that aftermath and menace are no longer generating — the asphalt-flesh continuity, the salmon-pink dress, the risen plank. Their return only earns anything if the camera is somewhere genuinely new when they come back.

Accidents are still arriving on schedule — the barrier arms sealing the horizon, the rebar reading as fingers, the garment convergent with the sightline. Object-level attention remains sharp. But a well-placed accident inside a frontal frame at noon cannot by itself move a score that the frame geometry is already anchoring at 1 or 2.

The archive is ninety-eight works of sustained, disciplined attention; the question it is now putting back to you, without variation, is where the camera goes next.
